text:
The Ladies 2026: 42 pemain mulakan saingan pusingan pertama - Portal Berita RTM

SERI KEMBANGAN, 1 Oktober – Pusingan pertama Kejohanan Golf Wanita The Ladies 2026 menyaksikan 42 pemain mula beraksi seawal pukul 7.30 pagi tadi. Saingan kali ini turut menampilkan gandingan pemain profesional serta amatur seperti Allycia Gan, Liyana Durisic, Durriyah Damian dan Kelly Tan. Menurut The Mines Resort & Golf Club, matlamat utama kejohanan tersebut adalah untuk melahirkan lebih ramai pemain berwibawa tempatan. Kejohanan tersebut juga sebagai batu loncatan penting sebelum saingan bertaraf antarabangsa menjelang kejohanan Maybank Championship tidak lama lagi.

Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google

SHAH ALAM (Sept 30): Genneva Gold Sdn Bhd, the company behind a massive gold investment scam, has been wound up by the High Court here, which could see victims recouping their losses.  In her brief judgment on Wednesday, Justice Wan Fadhilah Nor Wan Idris found that the company, which had been convicted for unlawful deposit-taking, had lost its foundation as it had ceased operations for many years and lacked the licences and permits to resume its original business.  The court also noted the deficiencies in its records and that the company did not have a functioning board of directors.

HLB Islamic salur RM138,600 pembiayaan kepada melalui SURI Inspirasi

PETALING JAYA: HLB Islamic menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (SURI) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan Pengantaraan Berasaskan Nilai (VBI).  Inisiatif itu secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94 peratus serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) anjuran SURI.

CIMB IB says Malaysia could widen corporate tax base for Budget 2027, cut old deductions

CIMB IB says Malaysia could widen corporate tax base for Budget 2027, cut old deductions KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Malaysia could widen its corporate tax base by reviewing special and double deductions that have been in place for two to three decades, and remove deductions that no longer serve their original purpose, said CIMB Investment Bank. CIMB IB said, citing KPMG senior adviser on tax policy Dr Verrinderjeet Singh during a discussion, that the removal of selected deductions could lead to the government collecting more revenue while creating room for a lower headline corporate tax rate.

Maybank, Hong Leong Win Best CEO and CFO Honours at Bursa Malaysia Awards

Bursa Malaysia awarded its top CEO and CFO honours to Maybank’s Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli and Hong Leong Bank’s Malkit Singh Maan. The inaugural Bursa Malaysia IR Awards 2026 took place on 4 September. Maybank received four honours, including Best CEO in Investor Relations for its President and Group CEO Khairussaleh. The bank also won Best Company in Investor Relations overall, Best Financial Reporting and Best Large-cap Company in Investor Relations for Financial Services. Malkit won Best CFO in Investor Relations.

AEON Credit Closes in on One-year Low as 2Q Results Underwhelm Investors, Analysts

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 30): AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd (KL:AEONCR) fell to its lowest in nearly a year while analysts turned cautious following a weaker-than-expected quarter at the consumer finance firm. At least two research houses downgraded the stock post-results. Earnings in the first-half only accounted for about one-third of the consensus’ full-year forecast, and there are now concerns over rising provisions and write-offs of bad loans going forward.

text:
RHB, The Makeover Guys Offer Flexi Loan for Home Purchase and Renovation

RHB Bank has partnered with renovation firm The Makeover Guys to offer financing that covers both a property purchase and renovation costs. The Makeover Flexi Loan provides eligible customers with financing of up to 120% of the property’s value. This comprises up to 90% for the home purchase and an additional 30% for renovation work, mortgage insurance or takaful, legal costs and documentation fees. Borrowers can repay the loan over a maximum of 35 years or until they reach the age of 70, whichever comes first.
